question: does the raw-paragraph layer lift product-path retrieval (the retrieval precondition of the 0.797 -> >=0.8045 parity target)?
design: product write_text -> orchestrated query, 20 questions seed 17 (same selection as the C2 probe); base arm = MEMPLEX_RAW_PARAGRAPH_LAYER=0, raw arm = layer on (completed in full under the MPS chunk clamp); metric session-level gold recall@8.

results.base_cross_check: identical to the C2 probe's base arm on the same questions

findings: NEGATIVE at top-8: joining verbatim paragraphs into the same ranked pool as extraction nodes DILUTES recall (0.85 -> 0.70). The mirror of the v13 slot lesson - in a mixed pool the raw unit does not always outrank the extraction node, and 8 slots amplify the crowding.
The harness (0.8045) seeded ONLY raw session units - no mixed-pool competition; the product path mixes both, which is the structural difference this probe exposes.

Metric-scope caveat: the probe scores top-8; the product/harness answer pipeline consumes top-24, where crowding pressure is lower - the answer-level parity run is the decisive instrument (in flight).
Likely fixes if parity confirms harm: paragraph fallback/quota in fusion (join only when extraction hits are weak, or reserve slots), or paragraph-only retrieval with extraction as a secondary leg.
honest_reading: n=20, CI roughly +/-14pp; the -15pp direction is consistent across 3 down / 0 up flips. MPS chunk clamp (16-chunk / 8192-char) carried the raw arm through the previously-fatal question 6, but the backend still wedged under 3-way sharding and once single-process the next morning - the parity run therefore executes on the CPU device (numerically near-identical vectors, disclosed).
